'''Nashitomi no Mikoto''' (梨迹臣命, birth and death dates unknown) was an ancient Japanese noble and ancestor of the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|ar|ناكاتومي|de|Nakatomi (Klan)|el|Αδελφότητα Νακατόμι|es|Clan Nakatomi|fa|خاندان ناکاتومی|fr|Clan Nakatomi|it|Clan Nakatomi|ja|中臣氏|ko|나카토미씨|nl|Nakatomi-clan|pl|Nakatomi (ród)|pt|Clã Nakatomi|vi|Gia tộc Nakatomi|zh|中臣氏|qid=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}. He is also known by the names Nashifu no Mikoto, Nashitsu no Mikoto, and Nashitomi.

== Overview ==
Although Nashitomi no Mikoto does not appear in the *{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}}* or *{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}*, he is mentioned in the *{{ill|Ōmi no Kuni Fudoki|ja|近江国風土記|zh|近江國風土記|qid=Q11638480}}*. According to the text, he was the second son of {{ill|Igatsuomi no Mikoto|ja|伊賀津臣命|qid=Q109599098}}, who had two sons and two daughters with a celestial maiden in the {{ill|Swan maiden|ar|فتاة البجعة|as|হংসকন্যা|bcl|Swan maiden|de|Schwanenjungfrau|es|Doncella cisne|fr|Femme-cygne|gan|羽衣仙女|it|Fanciulla cigno|ja|羽衣伝説|kcg|Fi̱ng nggwoneam a̱gwagwa|ko|날개옷 설화|ne|स्वान मेइडन|pt|Donzela-cisne|ru|Лебединые девы|tl|Swan maiden|uk|Діва-лебідь|vi|Tiên nữ thiên nga|zh|天鵝少女|qid=Q1326754|lt=Hagoromo}} associated with {{ill|Lake Yogo|ja|余呉湖|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Lake Yogo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11385251}} in {{ill|Ōmi Province|ca|Província d'Ōmi|ckb|پارێزگای ئۆمی|cs|Provincie Ómi|de|Provinz Ōmi|es|Provincia de Ōmi|fa|ولایت اومی|fi|Ōmin provinssi|fr|Province d'Ōmi|gl|Provincia de Ōmi|hak|Ōmi-koet|id|Provinsi Ōmi|it|Ōmi|ja|近江国|ko|오미국|lt|Omio žemė|nl|Omi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Ōmi|pt|Província de Ōmi|ru|Оми (провинция)|simple|Ōmi Province|sk|Ómi (provincia)|sr|Провинција Оми|tr|Ōmi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Омі|vi|Tỉnh Ōmi|zh|近江國|zh_min_nan|Ômi-kok|zh_yue|近江國|qid=Q843882|lt=Ōmi Province}}, Ikagō District.<ref name="fudoki">Yoshirō Akimoto, *Nihon Koten Bungaku Taikei Shinsōban Fudoki* (Iwanami Shoten, 1993), pp. 457-458.</ref>

Nashitomi no Mikoto is enshrined as a deity at the *{{ill|Omi Shrine (Yogo)|ja|乃彌神社|lt=Noimi Shrine}}*, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} in Ōmi Province, where he is worshipped alongside his brother Omishiru no Mikoto at the *{{ill|Omi Shrine (Yogo)|ja|乎彌神社|lt=Omi Shrine}}*, which incorporated Noimi Shrine. Additionally, he is also enshrined at *{{ill|Ōfura Shrine|ja|意富布良神社}}* as a subordinate deity.

== Genealogy ==
Nashitomi no Mikoto was the son of {{ill|Igatsuomi no Mikoto|ja|伊賀津臣命|qid=Q109599098}} and father of {{ill|Kamikikikatsu|ja|神聞勝命|qid=Q106106971|lt=Kamikikikatsu no Mikoto}}. His descendants include prominent clans such as the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|ar|ناكاتومي|de|Nakatomi (Klan)|el|Αδελφότητα Νακατόμι|es|Clan Nakatomi|fa|خاندان ناکاتومی|fr|Clan Nakatomi|it|Clan Nakatomi|ja|中臣氏|ko|나카토미씨|nl|Nakatomi-clan|pl|Nakatomi (ród)|pt|Clã Nakatomi|vi|Gia tộc Nakatomi|zh|中臣氏|qid=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}, {{ill|Ōnakatomi clan|ja|大中臣氏}}, and {{ill|Fujiwara clan|en|Fujiwara clan|qid=Q641628|lt=Fujiwara clan}}.

The *{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}* identifies him as the ancestor of the Kawamatauji no Muraji of {{ill|Kawachi Province|en|Kawachi Province|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi Province}}.
